correctness.rationale: At d=0 the renormalised traces are ±s^(2^n) and F_n=S_n^2(2−S_n), making the desired zero simple in s. The determinant entries equal d^(2^n), so the first derivatives vanish for n≥1. The two trace derivatives solve an explicit 2×2 recurrence with eigenvalues 2 and −1, yielding exactly the stated all-depth coefficient. At n=1, F_d=0, F_dd=12, F_s=−8√2, so the quadratic coefficient is 3√2/8. Signs of F_(n−1), F_(n+1), together with the published component theorem, prove the local 2^n versus 2^(n−1) distinction. The standalone verifier checked the exact n=1 derivatives, trace recursion through n=8 and 18 high-precision roots of the original equations. Fixed-depth limits only.

Their full relevant sections were inspected and compared by equations and mathematical implication. They do not state the exact symmetric-plane first-order response for arbitrary depth or the isolated second-order tangency. The result is expressly framed as an additional quantitative corollary of known implicit surfaces, not as discovery of those surfaces.

value.rationale: Connected-component doubling is a natural quantitative organizing structure of robust chaos in the Lozi map. The first boundary has zero transverse slope and positive quadratic drift, in sharp contrast with the negative linear drift of every subsequent fixed-depth boundary. This proves a parameter-geometry distinction between the first cascade step and all deeper ones and gives an explicit parity-resolved sensitivity of infinitely many natural bifurcation curves, rather than an arbitrary finite calculation.
